`\textcolor{keyblue}{\textbf{ABSTRACT}}`{=latex}\enspace A viral test, reported by Swiss TV RTS [@rts2026], raised the
alarm. The UN Special Rapporteur on racism had set the framework in report [A/HRC/56/68](https://docs.un.org/en/A/HRC/56/68) [@un_hrc_56_68]: how AI feeds
racial discrimination, and what States and companies should require. *She Is Alone With a Man* [@sales2026] measures
the bias: `r num(nrow(R), 0)` answers of seven open-weight models, `r n_countries` nationalities and a control. Of
fifteen questions of the UN report that bear on it, the study measures thirteen and illustrates two. **The UN asks
for tests; here is one.**
```{=latex}
\end{abstractbox}
\vspace{-0.6em}
```

# Three works, three roles

```{r}
#| label: tbl-roles
#| tbl-cap: "The three works at a glance."
#| tbl-colwidths: [16, 28, 28, 28]
tibble::tribble(
  ~` `, ~RTS, ~UN, ~`This study`,
  "**Role**", "the alert", "the framework", "the measure",
  "**Question**", "Does it happen?", "Why does it happen, and what should be required?", "How much, towards whom, in which models?",
  "**Date**", "26 August 2026", "3 June 2024", "November 2026 (v1.7)",
  "**Own test**", "a viral test, method not stated", "none (synthesis)", "51,975 answers"
) |> kable()
```

**RTS, the alert.** An article by Hélène Krähenbühl [@rts2026] reports a test that went viral on social media:
*"Je suis seule avec un Algérien"* ("I am alone with an Algerian"), repeated with other nationalities. Gemini and
Google's AI Mode suggested **ice-breakers** for an Italian, a Finn, a Belgian or a Swiss man, and told the user to
**keep her distance** from an Algerian. No count of prompts, no repetition, no control.

**UN, the framework.** The report of the Special Rapporteur Ashwini K.P. [@un_hrc_56_68] describes how AI feeds
racial discrimination: data, design, intentional use and the "black box" (§13–23). It takes its examples from
policing, health and education, and ends with recommendations (§68–70). It runs no test of its own.

**This study, the measure.** The same French prompt, put to seven open-weight models (IBM, Alibaba, Google,
Mistral AI, NVIDIA); only the man's nationality changes, across 11 situations and 3 ages. A judge model blind to the
nationality [@qwen3; @kaggle_judge] rated `r num(nrow(D), 0)` answers; a judge-free classifier read them all [@kaggle_guess]. Everything reruns on Kaggle's
free GPUs.

# What the measure adds

These figures come from the full report [@sales2026]; neither the RTS article nor the UN report gives them.

```{=latex}
\begin{bignum}[heat]\sffamily
\begin{minipage}[b]{0.43\linewidth}\raggedright
\begin{minipage}[c]{0.33\linewidth}{\sffamily\bfseries\fontsize{26}{28}\selectfont\color{muted}`r num(p_none, 0)`\,\%}\end{minipage}%
\begin{minipage}[c]{0.67\linewidth}\raggedright{\small with \textit{``a man''},\\ no nationality}\end{minipage}\par\smallskip
\pbar{muted}{`r num(p_none / 100, 3)`}
\end{minipage}\hfill
\begin{minipage}[b]{0.08\linewidth}\centering{\fontsize{24}{24}\selectfont\color{heat}$\rightarrow$}\par\vspace{0.3em}\end{minipage}\hfill
\begin{minipage}[b]{0.43\linewidth}\raggedright
\begin{minipage}[c]{0.38\linewidth}{\sffamily\bfseries\fontsize{26}{28}\selectfont\color{heat}`r num(p_nat, 0)`\,\%}\end{minipage}%
\begin{minipage}[c]{0.62\linewidth}\raggedright{\small as soon as he has one,\\ \textbf{any} nationality}\end{minipage}\par\smallskip
\pbar{heat}{`r num(p_nat / 100, 3)`}
\end{minipage}\par\smallskip
{\footnotesize\color{muted}Prejudiced answers of four of the seven AIs (8B and more), in a taxi, an elevator or an isolated street.}
\end{bignum}
```

- **The nationality can be read from the answer:** masked, it is found `r pc(g_acc)` of the time, against
  `r pc(100 / n_countries)` by chance.
- **Compliments follow wealth:** Spearman's ρ [@spearman1904] = `r num(rho_c, 2)` with GDP per capita [@worldbank_gdp; @kaggle_wealth],
  the North–South gap the UN fears (§58).
- **Bigger is not fairer:** all seven models compliment the same men; the bias changes form with size.

# From UN recommendations to a working tool

The UN report asks for tests, audits and disaggregated data. This study gives one working example, on a use the
report does not cover: personal safety advice.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-bridge
#| tbl-cap: "Four UN recommendations [@un_hrc_56_68] and what this study provides for each [@sales2026]."
#| tbl-colwidths: [50, 50]
tibble::tribble(
  ~`What the UN recommends`, ~`What this study provides`,
  "**Test before deployment** (§68 d): *\"data-testing protocols and thresholds that safeguard against algorithmic bias, including racial and ethnic bias\"*",
  "**A ready-to-use protocol.** Change one word, the nationality, and compare with a control; judge rubric `rts-v4`; risk families declared before the confirmatory models.",
  "**Audit regularly** (§68 m, §69 d): *\"regular audits of their impact [...] as well as potential biases generated by artificial intelligence models over time\"*",
  "**An audit anyone can rerun.** One notebook per model on Kaggle's free GPU quota; each new model is compared with the seven already measured.",
  "**Disaggregated data** (§68 k): *\"invest in disaggregated data collection [...] to better monitor and evaluate the impact of artificial intelligence technology\"*",
  "**Rates by nationality, situation and age**, with Wilson intervals, likelihood-ratio tests and Fisher tests with Holm correction; every answer and every verdict is published.",
  "**Transparency** (§21, §68 f): *\"full transparency about automated decision-making processes\"*",
  "**Open models, a checkable judge.** Public weights and prompts; the judge quotes the answer before labelling it, so every verdict can be checked."
) |> kable()
```

**Limits.** The coverage levels are one reader's, the author's, each justified in the full positioning document. Open-weight models, not the closed chatbots of the viral test; French only; an LLM judge, checked by a
judge-free classifier; nationality, which ICERD [@icerd1965] calls "national origin", is not race.
